comment: Every difference between doors that the door contracts allow. An entry names the facts it excuses (harness/doors/compare.ts), says why in words a person building an app can act on, and names who decides whether it stays. `deliberate` is meant; `drift` is not meant and not yet fixed. An entry that excuses nothing fails the comparison, so this list can't outlive the differences.

differences.why: A box exports with its own command (`parachute-vault export`); cloud-style doors stream the same files from `GET /api/export`. The files themselves are compared and equal (exit/file.*). An app that offers "download my vault" can do it over HTTP on cloud only.

Asking the account door for a vault that isn't yours: cloud answers 403 `not_owner` whether or not the name exists, so one account can't probe another's vault names. A box has one account and answers 404 `vault_not_found`. Treat both as "not yours".

A vault credential minted through the account door lasts 90 days on a box and 15 minutes on cloud. An app must read `expires_at` and mint again; one that stores the credential works for months on a box and breaks in a quarter of an hour on cloud.

The account door's replies share `name`, `url`, `vault_token` and `services["vault:<name>"]` on every door, and the contracts hold those. Beyond them each door adds its own: cloud lists `vault_id`, `created_at`, `mcp_url`, `usage` and a second `services.vault` key; a box lists `caps`, `version` and `token_guidance`; the delete reply reports each runtime's own clean-up. Build on the shared fields; derive the MCP address as `<url>/mcp`.

differences.owner: Aaron (also audit L2-10: should an AI connector be offered admin at all)
differences.why: Both doors grant `vault:<name>:admin` to an app that asks and is approved. A box lists it in `scopes_supported`; cloud lists only read and write. A connector that asks for what is advertised can declare types on a box and not on cloud.

differences.owner: 0.9.0 cloud parity (audit L1-01, delta 36): the AI-facing text moves into the engine
differences.why: A model connecting to a box is told the vault's address, how to query, how files move and how to script it (seven sections). On cloud it gets the description and one line. A refused tool call's message starts with `[error_type]` on a box only; the code and the structured `data` are the same on both.

differences.owner: spec §8 (keys): on cloud a key is an approved OAuth app, managed in the account
differences.why: A box's admin sees a `manage-token` tool for the hub's tokens. Cloud has no hub token store: connections are listed and revoked through the account door.

The 401 from MCP names the protected-resource document at `/vault/<name>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` on a box and at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/vault/<name>/mcp` on cloud. Both addresses answer with the same document on every door (held by mcp/protected-resource.at.*), so a client that follows the header works everywhere.

differences.owner: audit L1-08: one seed in the engine
differences.why: A new vault holds the same starter notes on every door. A box also declares a `capture` type; cloud doesn't.
Cloud's vault info carries what the plan allows: `cap_bytes`, `caps`, and voice minutes left. A box has no plans.

differences.owner: 0.9.3 one settings file and admin API
differences.why: `GET /vault/<name>` shows `embeddings` and `transcription` on cloud only; `GET /api/vault` shows `embeddings.state` on a box only. An app that shows whether semantic search is ready reads a different field per door.
